title: Cabinet Approves Establishment of IN-SPACe
description: The Union Cabinet approved the creation of the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe) as an autonomous single-window nodal agency under the Department of Space. This decision formally opened the Indian space sector to non-governmental entities (NGEs) by providing equal access to ISRO infrastructure and establishing an independent regulatory body.
actors: Union Cabinet, Department of Space, ISRO

title: Expansion of NSIL Mandate as Commercial Aggregator
description: Alongside the creation of IN-SPACe, NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) was re-mandated to transition from a passive marketing arm to a primary commercial operator. Under the new mandate, NSIL builds and owns operational satellites, aggregates commercial launch services, and transfers ISRO-developed technologies to private industry.
actors: Department of Space, NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), ISRO

title: Publication of Draft Space Activities Bill 2017
description: The Department of Space published the initial draft of the Space Activities Bill 2017 to invite public comments. The draft proposed a licensing framework for commercial space operations, third-party liability rules, and penal provisions for unauthorized space activities.

title: Revision of Draft Space Activities Bill
description: Following stakeholder feedback and Cabinet approval of IN-SPACe, the Department of Space revised the proposed legislative text to shift regulatory oversight from the Ministry directly to IN-SPACe while refining indemnification clauses.

title: IN-SPACe Grants Maiden Authorization to Dhruva Space
description: IN-SPACe granted its first-ever formal authorization to private space firm Dhruva Space for testing its Satellite Orbital Deployer (DSOD-1U) onboard ISRO's PSLV-C53 POEM orbital platform. This marked the operational start of private payload authorizations in India.

title: IN-SPACe Authorizes Digantara Space Weather Payload
description: IN-SPACe authorized Digantara Research and Technologies to integrate and fly its ROBI space weather sensor payload on ISRO's PSLV-C53 mission. The authorization validated private environmental monitoring payloads in low Earth orbit.

title: Establishment of India's First Private Launchpad
description: IN-SPACe and ISRO authorized Agnikul Cosmos to set up India's first private launchpad and dedicated mission control center (Dhanush) inside the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota. The facility enables private NGEs to run independent launch ops.

title: Authorization for Maiden Private Rocket Launch
description: IN-SPACe issued authorization for Skyroot Aerospace to execute Mission Prarambh, granting permission for the sub-orbital launch of the Vikram-S rocket from Sriharikota with three customer payloads.

title: Maiden Launch of Private Sub-Orbital Rocket Vikram-S
description: Skyroot Aerospace successfully launched Vikram-S from Sriharikota, achieving India's first private rocket flight. The mission demonstrated 3D-printed avionics, composite rocket structures, and solid propulsion systems under IN-SPACe supervision.

title: Union Cabinet Approves Indian Space Policy 2023
description: The Cabinet Committee on Security approved the Indian Space Policy 2023, laying down an overarching framework that encourages private sector participation across all space domains, from satellite operations to space resource exploration.
actors: Union Cabinet, Cabinet Committee on Security, Department of Space

title: Formal Publication of Indian Space Policy 2023
description: The Department of Space publicly released the official text of the Indian Space Policy 2023. The policy codifies the role of ISRO as an R&D agency, NSIL as commercial aggregator, and IN-SPACe as an autonomous regulator and promoter for NGEs.

title: India Signs the Artemis Accords
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi signed the Artemis Accords during a state visit to Washington D.C., making India the 27th signatory. The signing aligns India with multilateral norms for peaceful civil space exploration and lunar commercial governance.
actors: Government of India, NASA, US Department of State

title: Release of IN-SPACe Norms Guidelines and Procedures NGP
description: IN-SPACe published comprehensive Norms Guidelines and Procedures (NGP) detailing eligibility, application workflows, liability requirements, and safety norms for NGE authorizations across satellites, ground stations, and launch systems.

title: Cabinet Approval of Liberalized FDI Policy for Space
description: The Union Cabinet approved key amendments to the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Policy for the space sector, creating clear entry routes: 74% automatic for satellite manufacturing, 49% automatic for launch vehicles, and 100% automatic for satellite components.
actors: Union Cabinet, DPIIT, Department of Space

title: Notification of Amended FEMA FDI Rules for Space
description: The Ministry of Finance notified Press Note 1 of 2024 under Foreign Exchange Management (Non-debt Instruments) Rules, operationalizing 100% FDI caps and sub-sector automatic clearance thresholds effective April 16, 2024.
actors: Ministry of Finance, Reserve Bank of India, DPIIT

title: Successful Sub-Orbital Test of Agnikul Agnibaan SOrTeD
description: Agnikul Cosmos conducted the successful maiden flight of its Agnibaan SOrTeD launch vehicle from its private launchpad at Sriharikota. The flight successfully flight-tested India's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.

title: Authorization of Ground Station as a Service GSaaS
description: IN-SPACe granted commercial authorization to Dhruva Space to establish and operate ground stations for Telemetry, Tracking, and Command (TTC) services, expanding private space infrastructure authorization types.

title: Cabinet Approves 1000 Crore Venture Capital Fund for Space
description: The Union Cabinet approved a dedicated 1000 Crore Venture Capital Fund under the aegis of IN-SPACe. The fund aims to catalyze private space startups by providing capital across early-stage and growth-stage funding rounds over five years.
actors: Union Cabinet, IN-SPACe, Department of Space

title: IN-SPACe Authorization for Privately Led EO Constellation
description: IN-SPACe executed a formal agreement authorizing a Pixxel-led consortium of Indian firms (including Dhruva Space and SatSure) to design, build, and operate India's first privately-built national Earth Observation constellation.

title: Orbital Launch Authorization and Mission Aagaman
description: IN-SPACe authorized Skyroot Aerospace's maiden orbital flight of the Vikram-1 rocket under Mission Aagaman, deploying commercial small satellites into low Earth orbit and establishing operational orbital authorization protocols.

title: Enactment of Commercial Space Launch Act of 1984
description: The US Congress enacted the Commercial Space Launch Act (CSLA) to promote, facilitate, and regulate commercial space launch operations. The law designated the Department of Transportation (later transferred to FAA/AST) as the primary launch licensing authority.

title: Enactment of US Commercial Space Launch Competitiveness Act
description: US Congress enacted Public Law 114-90 (HR 2262), granting US citizens explicit statutory rights to commercially explore, extract, and own space resources. The act also extended learning periods for commercial human spaceflight safety regulations.
actors: US Congress, Executive Office of the President

title: Issuance of Space Policy Directive-1
description: President Donald Trump signed Space Policy Directive-1, instructing NASA to lead an innovative lunar exploration program in partnership with commercial entities and international allies, laying the groundwork for the Artemis Program.
actors: Executive Office of the President, NASA

title: Establishment of the Artemis Accords
description: NASA and the US Department of State, along with 7 founding international partner nations, unveiled the Artemis Accords. The framework establishes non-binding principles for civil space exploration, resource extraction, and deconfliction zones.

title: FAA Streamlined Launch and Reentry Licensing Rules Part 450
description: The Federal Aviation Administration published 14 CFR Part 450, consolidating legacy launch licensing rules into a single performance-based regulatory framework for commercial launch and reentry operations.

title: Launch of SpaceResources.lu Initiative
description: The Ministry of the Economy of Luxembourg launched the SpaceResources.lu initiative, creating a strategic public framework to attract commercial space resource exploration firms through capital co-investments and legal clarity.

title: Passage of Luxembourg Space Resources Law
description: Luxembourg Parliament passed the Law on the Exploration and Use of Space Resources, becoming the first nation in Europe to explicitly affirm that space resources are capable of being owned by commercial entities registered in Luxembourg.
actors: Luxembourg Parliament, Ministry of the Economy

title: Formal Creation of Luxembourg Space Agency
description: Luxembourg established the Luxembourg Space Agency (LSA) to accelerate business development, administer national space economic development funds, and supervise commercial licensing under national space laws.
actors: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy, LSA

title: Luxembourg Joins Artemis Accords as Founding Signatory
description: Luxembourg signed the Artemis Accords as one of eight original founding countries, cementing multilateral support for transparent commercial space resource exploitation.
actors: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy, LSA, NASA

title: Establishment of the UAE Space Agency
description: The UAE President issued a Federal Decree-Law establishing the UAE Space Agency to develop national space infrastructure, regulate commercial satellites, and lead the Emirates Mars Mission (Hope Probe).

title: Approval of UAE National Space Policy
description: The UAE Cabinet approved the National Space Policy to provide strategic guidance for commercial space investments, spectrum allocation, and scientific space exploration.

title: Enactment of UAE Federal Space Law No 12 of 2019
description: The UAE enacted Federal Law No. 12 of 2019 regarding the regulation of the space sector, creating a single-window licensing system, operator liability rules, space mining rights, and foreign ownership guidelines.

title: UAE Joins Artemis Accords as Founding Signatory
description: The UAE Space Agency signed the Artemis Accords as a founding international partner, advancing cooperation in deep space exploration, lunar logistics, and interoperability.

title: Issuance of Space Activity Permitting Regulations
description: The UAE Space Agency published comprehensive executive regulations governing authorization processes for launch operations, satellite telecommunications, orbit allocations, and space safety protocols.
